text: emily_support: Heads-up — ACME (private deployment) is getting a 403 when the collector tries to upload the debug bundle after redaction. Ticket #ACME-12345. Collector v1.9.2 on k8s behind a MinIO gateway. Customer reports request-id header: X-ACME-REQ-98765. Attaching shortened collector log excerpt below and a curl they used. emily_support: ``` 2026-03-10T14:12:33Z collector INFO redaction completed, ruleset v2.1 2026-03-10T14:12:33Z collector INFO bundle created: bundle-acme-20260310.tar.gz (78MB) 2026-03-10T14:12:34Z uploader WARN upload failed, status=403, request-id=X-ACME-REQ-98765, msg=AccessDenied 2026-03-10T14:12:34Z uploader DEBUG upload-url=https://minio.acme.internal/support-uploads/ACME/bundle-acme-20260310.tar.gz ``` emily_support: Customer ran this curl to reproduce: emily_support: ``` curl -v -X PUT \n -H "Content-Type: application/octet-stream" \n -H "x-amz-meta-redaction:v2.1" \n --data-binary @bundle-acme-20260310.tar.gz \n "https://minio.acme.internal/support-uploads/ACME/bundle-acme-20260310.tar.gz?X-Amz-Signature=..." ``` rafael_oncall: Thanks Emily. Two quick asks to repro: 1) can we see the exact presign URL (redact token) and TTL the collector requested; 2) the full S3 error body (XML) if available — sometimes MinIO returns SignatureDoesNotMatch vs AccessDenied which changes the root cause. morgan_infra: Also confirm collector config: redaction_rules path + manifest generation mode (we recently changed line-ending handling in manifest v2). If the manifest SHA the presign was generated against differs from the bundle bytes (LF vs CRLF), MinIO will reject the PUT with a signature mismatch. emily_support: Copying the manifest header from collector logs (redacted): emily_support: ``` manifest: { "bundle_name": "bundle-acme-20260310.tar.gz", "sha256": "REDACTED_SHA", "generator_version": "man-gen-2026-02-28", "manifest_mode": "v2-lf" } ``` sre_bot: Collector metadata: version=1.9.2, node=k8s-prod-3, kernel=5.10.127, os=ubuntu-22.04, python=3.10.8. Network: egress via NAT gateway ngw-prod-4. rafael_oncall: That manifest_mode="v2-lf" is interesting — if the presign was created from a manifest with CRLF handling on the upload service, signature will not match. Emily, can you ask Tom (ACME) to: 1) run a local reproducer that downloads the presign URL and re-uploads using --upload-file (we want to see whether their client or our presign is the problem); 2) paste the full XML error body returned by MinIO. emily_support: I asked Tom and he pasted the XML error: emily_support: ``` SignatureDoesNotMatch The request signature we calculated does not match the signature you provided. X-ACME-REQ-98765 minio-1 ``` morgan_infra: Ok that's a signature mismatch. Next steps: 1) reproduce locally by fetching presign and re-uploading with curl (emily sent curl, but make sure not to double-encode querystring); 2) verify the presign was generated against the final redacted bundle bytes. If ACME's collector redaction changed after presign generation (race), they'll send different bytes. rafael_oncall: Emily — please gather the following from the customer and attach to the debug bundle: - collector-config.yaml - the exact presign request (headers + path) from the collector log (the GET to /presign) - uploader logs with full debug (include X-Request-Id) - a short curl reproduction (we'll paste ours) emily_support: Asking Tom now. Also note ACME cannot open outbound 443 to our public endpoint due to policy, so they use an internal MinIO endpoint. If this is MinIO's presign implementation quirk, we might need to re-sign using their server-side signing method. morgan_infra: If customer can't reach our S3 endpoint and they have an SFTP drop, offer an SFTP fallback: redaction must run locally first (important). Provide these steps: morgan_infra: ``` # run redaction locally (collector binary) ./collector generate-bundle --config /etc/collector/config.yml --output bundle-acme-20260310.tar.gz # verify redaction rules applied ./collector inspect bundle-acme-20260310.tar.gz --check-redaction # scp to our support bastion (if customer allows) scp -i /home/tom/.ssh/support_key bundle-acme-20260310.tar.gz support@bastion.support.redwood.example.com:/incoming/acme/ # OR sftp (preferred for restricted networks) sftp -i /home/tom/.ssh/support_key support@bastion.support.redwood.example.com < collector.journal.log # collector verbose run to reproduce\./collector --config /etc/collector/config.yml --debug bundle --output reproduce-bundle.tar.gz 2>&1 | tee reproduce-run.log # manifest SHA check sha256sum reproduce-bundle.tar.gz | awk '{print $1}' > reproduce.sha256 ``` emily_support: Tom uploaded the files to the SFTP we provided. I pulled them down and verified the reproduce.sha256 differs from the manifest sha in the presign. Looks like a manifest generation mismatch. morgan_infra: Good find. Two mitigation options: 1) re-generate presign from the node that produced the bundle (same line-ending and tar tool), or 2) support will accept the SFTP-uploaded bundle and we re-sign server-side and move into the support store. Which does ACME prefer? emily_support: ACME is ok with SFTP fallback for now. I've asked infra to perform server-side re-sign and ingest. Rafael, can you take the server-side step? I'll attach the SFTP path and request-id. rafael_oncall: Taking it. I'll run the following: fetch bundle from SFTP, verify sha, re-sign manifest using support-signing tool (with miner_key_v3), PUT to support store, and confirm object accessible. I'll paste logs when done. sre_bot: Action logged: incident:ACME-12345 fallback:sftp-ingest assigned_to:rafael_oncall due:2026-03-10T15:02:00Z emily_support: Thanks everyone — I'll update the customer and close the loop once Rafael confirms the ingest. Tom said he also captured network tcpdump around the failed PUT; I'll attach that if needed. :raised_hands: rafael_oncall: Done — bundle ingested, re-signed, object is available at support://store/ingested/ACME/bundle-acme-20260310.tar.gz. Verified manifest sha matches. Closing this path; will follow up with infra to add presign manifest-mode check to the presign endpoint to prevent mismatches going forward. emily_support: Awesome, closing ticket after customer confirmation. :white_check_mark:
